item.text:
Both vehicles are configured as the same MOOS community on the same MOOSDB port, so they collide conceptually. Each vehicle needs its own MOOSDB, with a unique port and a unique community name.

For example:

```text
// first vehicle file
ServerHost = localhost
ServerPort = 9001
Community  = alpha
```

```text
// second vehicle file
ServerHost = localhost
ServerPort = 9002
Community  = bravo
```

The shoreside should run as its own MOOS community on a third port, for example:

```text
// shoreside
ServerHost = localhost
ServerPort = 9000
Community  = shoreside
```

Then configure the communication bridges so shoreside knows it is receiving reports from `alpha` and `bravo`, not two processes both claiming to be the same community.
